adviceById.D1: Choose interesting, interacting characters without making information overwhelmingly strong.
adviceById.seating: Assign the chosen characters to seats; do not change the character set.
adviceById.D2: Choose an absent Townsfolk character. Never reveal that this player is the Drunk.
adviceById.D3: In 5–6 player games, consider making the Fortune Teller their own red herring.
adviceById.D4: Both information targets exclude the recipient. Choose only an enumerated truthful possibility.
adviceById.D5: Both targets exclude the recipient. Zero is legal only when no Outsider can be detected.
adviceById.D6: Both information targets exclude the recipient. Choose only an enumerated truthful possibility.
adviceById.D7: The official suggestion is two Townsfolk and one Outsider; every candidate is a legal absent-good bluff set.
adviceById.D8: False information is usually appropriate, but truth is allowed. Make it plausible and consistent with evil bluffs; never reveal impairment.
adviceById.D10: Choose an interesting registration without abusing it. Alignment and character are independent and fixed for the game.
adviceById.D11: Do not overuse misregistration. Alignment and character are independent and fixed for the game.
adviceById.D12: Consider keeping the Mayor alive until the final day, unless the group overwhelmingly trusts them.
adviceById.D13: Do not directly decide the winner by redirecting. Avoid frequently choosing dead, protected or Soldier targets for no death.
adviceById.D14: Choose a living true Minion. Mandatory Scarlet Woman succession is handled by the engine.
